questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That the subjects offered were along the lines of zoology as these type of courses are not available for bachelor students at KU.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy, the exchange student team here were really nice and very quick at answering emails and getting back to you.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was orientation, which wasn't super intense but gave you a brief idea and understanding of the layout of the campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite difficult. There were many accommodation places, however a lot of them didn't offer single semester accommodation. So that is something to keep in mind when starting to look.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Walking to everything and being a bit further away from campus meant that you had to time that and manage your time well.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I rated the registration process a bit lower only because this university had a weird process of choosing courses but then afterwards you had to make your own timetable of those courses and figure out yourself if there was any overlap. There often was and this meant it was a weird puzzle of trying to take courses that I still found interesting but also didn't overlap. I think in the end I had to rearrange and drop courses up to 5 times.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The team was very kind in helping you find courses that didn't overlap but it was just a very stressful time especially since classes also started and if you didn't have a course by that time you weren't sure if you were possibly missing class.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was overall quite successful. I was able to get 4/6 of the courses I wanted. One of them was listed as an option for semester 1 courses when I signed up in the spring but when I got here they had moved it to a semester 2 course which meant I had to choose something else. The other one was full and I had to choose a different but quite similar course. Overall I was happy with my classes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would advise to double check the courses, when they are available (semester 1 or 2) and double checking the timetable for any overlap. Also making sure that you have any prerequisites that might be mandatory.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses ranged from 1st year to 3rd year, which meant that sometimes I was in a class with students that had not studied for as long as I had. This meant that some of the courses were simpler, but it didn't matter to me because it served as a refresher course for myself and also put less pressure on knowing everything or learning everything for the first time.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I felt there was much less work somehow. Lectures didn't feel as long either. Maybe it is because I prefer English as my academic language, that I just felt I was learning better in this environment than I do at UCPH but that is my own issue. The second thing that I found here was they were much more focused on writing essays, which I feel is something UCPH is lacking. It is important for us students to also learn how to write scientific essays and the bachelor's project shouldn't be the first time people are learning how to write like that.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Forensic Psychology, Applied Cognition, French for Beginners, Adaptations to Extreme Environments, Practical Invertebrate Skills, Ecology and Zoology Literature Review

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The literature review class that I did was very good because it taught me how to write scientifically and do research properly. I chose the class on purpose to better prepare myself for the bachelor project, and I really feel like it has aided me in that sense.

questions.answer: NA

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: At this university they have a collaboration with a sports arena where students have free access to swimming pools, football fields, squash courts, inside courts, gym, etc. They also have free access to sign up for classes such as yoga, spin, etc. I was really happy to have this and was not expecting all of that to be free so I would say that sports and gym memberships was a lot less expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
At this university they have a collaboration with a sports arena where students have free access to swimming pools, football fields, squash courts, inside courts, gym, etc. They also have free access to sign up for classes such as yoga, spin, etc. I was really happy to have this and was not expecting all of that to be free so I would say that sports and gym memberships was a lot less expensive than expected. 

There were also plenty of societies to join and there were so many it was hard to decide between what to choose!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend joining some societies or clubs cause it really makes your social circle bigger and gives you an opportunity to meet more people that not only have the same interests as you but also are not living in the same place as you or in your classes, which means you have more variety in where you can meet people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There were many trips arranged by the international students society, these cost money but were so worth it because they take you out to experience more of the country. It was quite hard to get around in this host country especially if you didn't own a car as public transportation wasn't as common so this meant that being driven around in a big bus was a great option. Exploring the city center and the pubs and restaurants and cafes the city has to offer is also a great idea.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy. I've moved around a lot so doesn't take me long to get settled into a new country. Also because this was in Europe where we still see a lot of similarities.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It was definitely most difficult to do this but I'd say joining those clubs or societies is where you are most guaranteed to meet them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: NA

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The love of tea

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't mind the weather. Enjoy walking around because public transportation is horrible. Join the many clubs and societies that they have to offer.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: NA

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being able to meet new people, learn to live on my own in a different country and try new things.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Leaving, because saying goodbye is truly heartbreaking.

questions.answer: NA
